prs.title: feat(linter/typescript/await-thenable): support `allowMixedPromiseArrays` option
prs.author: camc314
prs.body: Add `allowMixedPromiseArrays` to `typescript/await-thenable`, following https://github.com/oxc-project/tsgolint/pull/1307. Oxlint now validates and forwards the option, and exposes it in the JSON schema and TypeScript config types. It defaults to `false`; when enabled, Promise aggregators accept mixed synchronous and Promise-like inputs while synchronous-only inputs still report errors.

prs.title: perf(tasks): build the coverage profile without cross-crate LTO
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
> AI disclosure: this PR, the measurements behind it, and this description were produced with Claude Code at a maintainer's request. It should get human review before it leaves draft.

## Summary

This PR does three things:
- **`Cargo.toml`:** `[profile.coverage]` changes from `lto = "thin"` to `lto = false`.
- **`AGENTS.md`:** adds an opt-in note on incremental compilation for this profile, with its measured cost.
- **`AGENTS.md`:** the `cargo coverage -- <tool>` examples become `cargo coverage <tool>`; the old form runs every suite.

## Why

With `lto = "thin"`, the library crates are compiled to bitcode only (`-C linker-plugin-lto`). The final binary (`-C lto=thin`) then re-optimizes and re-codegens the whole program on every rebuild. After a one-line `oxc_minifier` edit, `cargo build --timings` showed where the time went:

| | `oxc_minifier` lib | `oxc_minsize` lib | `oxc_minsize` bin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lto = "thin"` | 5.2s | 1.9s | **19.4s** (whole-program ThinLTO) |
| `lto = false` | 7.2s | 2.3s | **0.7s** (plain link) |

Every binary built with this profile pays that step separately. That covers the harnesses (`oxc_minsize`, `oxc_track_memory_allocations`, `oxc_coverage`) and the NAPI test builds (`pnpm build-test`). The profile's own comment says `lto = "thin"` was chosen for "faster compile time", and turning LTO off is faster still. The profile exists to run the harnesses with debug assertions, which doesn't need cross-crate LTO.

prs.title: fix(lsp): return default diagnostic report when server is not in pull mode
prs.author: Sysix
prs.body:
Addresses one problem in #27736.
Clients should respect the the `ServerCapabilities` from the `intialize` response.
When no `diagnosticProvider` is provided, the server says to the client that `textDocument/diagnostic` is not supported.

```
        /**
	 * The server has support for pull model diagnostics.
	 *
	 * @since 3.17.0
	 */
	diagnosticProvider?: DiagnosticOptions | DiagnosticRegistrationOptions;
```
_https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.18/specification/#pull-diagnostics_

Sadly the client does not need to respect them and can requzest `textDocument/diagnostic` even if we told him not to do.
To avoid duplicate linting processes on push mode (server is sending diagnostics to the client on `didOpen/didChange`, we check if we are in the right mode, or else bail out earlier.

prs.title: fix(linter): use the type-aware rule's severity when another plugin has a rule with the same name
prs.author: NavpreetSSidhu
prs.body:
Closes #28136

Severity for tsgolint diagnostics was looked up in the file's resolved rules by name only. `unicorn/prefer-string-starts-ends-with` has the same name as `typescript/prefer-string-starts-ends-with`, so whichever came first in the list won, and the order differs for files that match an `overrides` entry. Both lookups (CLI and `lint_source`) now only match type-aware rules.

Added a CLI fixture with the config from the issue; the snapshot shows a warning for both files, and it fails on main with an error for `b.tsx`. `cargo test -p oxlint --lib tsgolint`, `cargo test -p oxc_linter --lib`, clippy and fmt pass.

AI disclosure: I used Claude Code to help trace the cause and write the patch, and I reviewed and tested it myself.
